Cliopatria's County of Foix row is the Foix-Béarn-Navarre-Albret composite: its Béarn cells (from 1294) overlap the separate county-of-bearn dossier (found 1347, which reads Cliopatria's County of Béarn 1385-1452 as eastern Foix lands); its 1482 shape holds Périgord and Limousin cells while the Cliopatria Périgord row ends 1481; the House of Bourbon row takes the cells over in 1556. The reviewers of eu-10 should reconcile county-of-foix, county-of-bearn, county-of-perigord and house-of-bourbon.

Cliopatria's Capetian House of Anjou row keeps Anjou/Maine to 1325 and overlaps the County of Anjou (Valois) row from 1294; the dossier ends the Capetian hold in 1290 (Treaty of Senlis), as county-of-anjou already records, and ends the row in 1382 (house-of-valois-anjou records the 1382 gain).

Cliopatria rows end early for states that continued: Principality of Orange 1571 (pages: to 1713, extended by keyframe and contest 1672-1713), County of Artois 1332 (county to 1659; cells carried by free-county-of-burgundy 1333-1384), Dauphiné 1351 (sale 1349, distinct polity), County of Foix 1555 (county to 1607).
